title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 552 and 554): 𝔊 is a group, discrete or profinite; the notes fix the profinite case. Two elements ρ, σ are given. Put ε0 = σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = ρσ^{-1}. One checks ε1 = ρ ε0 ρ^{-1} = σ ε0 σ^{-1}; Grothendieck writes ρ(x), σ(x) for inner conjugation. Let L0 and L1 be the procyclic closed subgroups generated by ε0 and ε1.

For u ∈ Aut(𝔊), set ξ = [u,ρ] = u(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = [u,σ] = u(σ)σ^{-1}. The subgroup B̃'_0 consists of the u that:
- fix the conjugacy class of ρ,
- fix the conjugacy class of σ,
- normalize L0, i.e. u(ε0) ∈ L0, i.e. u(ε0) = ε0^ν.
These three conditions say exactly that the pair (ξ,η) lies in the set Σ (later R_{ρ,σ}) of pairs satisfying:
- ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} for some α,
- η = βσ(β)^{-1} for some β,
- η^{-1}ξ ∈ L1, i.e. ξ = η ε1^ν.
The map (36), u ↦ (ξ,η), is injective when ρ, σ topologically generate 𝔊.

On this page Grothendieck isolates a 'Hypothèse fondamentale' (37):
- (a) ρ, σ topologically generate 𝔊;
- (b) the map (36) is bijective.
Unpacked, (b) says: for every (α,β) with αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1} ε1^{ν'}, the assignment ρ ↦ αρα^{-1}, σ ↦ βσβ^{-1} extends to an automorphism u of 𝔊. That u then automatically lies in B̃'_0, and it is unique by (a).

Under (37), the set R_{ρ,σ} of solutions (ξ,η) inherits a group structure by transport of structure from B̃'_0. Implicitly the law is (ξ,η)·(ξ',η') = (ξ·u(ξ'), η·u(η')), since [uu',ρ] = u([u',ρ])·[u,ρ]. This is the same mechanism that gives the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld/Ihara) its law: f'' = f·u_f(f').

Purpose: in the 'équation des lacets' programme, this replaces 'automorphisms of the profinite π1 respecting inertia data' by 'solutions of an equation in 𝔊 × 𝔊'. The aim is to make the solution set itself a group, independent of Aut. The next page restarts the theory systematically with the groups M_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No outright error. Hypothesis (b) is stated as an axiom, not proved. For a free (profinite) group on ρ, σ it is a genuine non-trivial condition. The endomorphism ρ ↦ αρα^{-1}, σ ↦ βσβ^{-1} always exists in the free case, but surjectivity of the images is not automatic. Hopficity then gives bijectivity only once generation is known. So (b) amounts to a generation statement for conjugates satisfying the twisted relation ξ = η ε1^ν. Its validity for the groups of interest (free profinite F̂2, or Ẑ/2 * Ẑ/3-type groups, given the earlier remark σ^{-1}=σ) is left open on this page.

Minor notational looseness: [u,ρ] is written as a commutator in the semidirect product Aut(𝔊)⋉𝔊. Also 'a) b) c)' on the last lines refers to the three conditions defining Σ, numbered (5) on the next page, not to (37) a), b).

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms that fix the conjugacy classes of two generators and normalize the procyclic subgroup of their 'product' by the pair of 'commutator cocycles' (ξ,η) = ([u,ρ],[u,σ]). Characterizing the image by the equations ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}, η = βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}, ξ = η ε1^ν.
ideas.modern_name: Description of (a variant of) GT-type / braid-like automorphism groups of profinite free or triangle groups via solutions (f) of equations; Ihara's description of Out-type subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Lochak–Schneps for GT and its variants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the GT-type programme only vaguely; this explicit equation-level formalism appears only in these notes

ideas.what: 'Hypothèse fondamentale': bijectivity of u ↦ (ξ,η) onto the solution set, so that the solution set inherits a group law by transport of structure.
ideas.modern_name: Group structure on the set of solutions (λ,f) of the GT equations, with law f'' = f·u_f(f')

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates as an axiom that every 'twisted conjugation' solution (α,β), with αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ε1^{ν}, comes from an automorphism. No verification is given here of when this holds (e.g. for F̂2 or profinite triangle groups). This is precisely the subtle surjectivity/invertibility issue later handled for GT (the passage from the monoid of solutions to its invertible elements).
missed.quote: Hypothèse fondamentale sur 𝔊, muni de ρ,σ ... b) L'application (36) (injective par a)) est bijective.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, axiomatic formulation, independent of Drinfeld, of the problem 'when do solutions of the loop equations form a group'. A criterion for groups 𝔊 satisfying (37) would give a uniform construction of GT-like groups for other (ρ,σ)-data.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean unpublished precursor of the Drinfeld–Ihara mechanism, where solutions of equations in a profinite group become a group via the automorphisms they induce. It is consistent with what is already known about the Longue Marche follow-up notes, and here it is stated only as a hypothesis, without new results.
transcription_corrections: The last line should read 'de celle de B̃'_0', not 'B̃'_{ρσ}'. The subscript under B' appears to be 0 (the image shows something like B̃'_0 with a mark below).
The parenthetical should read '(on aura donc nécessairement u ∈ B̃'_0, et u sera unique par a))'.
Line: 'u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) i.e. u(ρ)=ξρ' — the struck-out fragment after it is illegible. Similarly 'u(σ) = int(β)σ i.e. u(σ)=ησ'.
'R_{ρ,σ}' is plausible; it denotes the set of (ξ,η) satisfying conditions a) b) c) = (5) of the next page.
